results.title: CurseForge vs Modrinth: Where to Get Mods Safely
results.content:
## Mods on your own server

On a Minecraft server at CakeHosting, the Mods section of the game panel searches Modrinth directly, and under Modpacks you install packs from Modrinth, CurseForge and Feed The Beast, among others, with the right loader included. The full walkthrough is in install mods and modpacks on your server, and running a modpack server with friends helps you pick a pack for your group. [...] With a modpack, everyone has to play exactly the same version. A CurseForge pack is a `.zip` with a manifest, and when importing, the CurseForge app by default only installs files that are genuinely hosted on CurseForge. Modrinth uses `.mrpack`, the only format you can upload to Modrinth. On Modrinth, every mod shows whether it belongs on the server, with the players or on both. Mods for visuals and performance, such as Sodium or shaders, only belong with the players. [...] Is CurseForge safe?

Yes. Every file goes through automated malware checks, and new versions of most projects are also reviewed by hand. The biggest risk is in files you get outside CurseForge, such as a zip sent over Discord.

  What’s the difference between CurseForge and Modrinth?

CurseForge hosts mods for many games and has its own app. Modrinth focuses only on Minecraft: Java Edition, is largely open source and gives creators 75 per cent of its advertising revenue.
